svg.title: Comparison of angular diameter of some celestial bodies
svg.desc: Comparison of angular diameter of the Sun, Moon and planets with the International Space Station and human visual acuity, compiled by CMG Lee. To get a true representation of the sizes, view the image at a distance of 103 [1 / tan(33.5/60 * pi/180)] times the width of the largest (Moon: max.) circle. For example, if this circle is 10 cm wide on your monitor, view it from 10.3 m away. Planetary angular diameters are from factsheets at http://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/ and Sun/Moon ones are from http://education.gsfc.nasa.gov/eclipse/pages/faq.html .
